Prevention: Plant healthy saplings originating from authorized nurseries.
Plant mandarin and sweet orange: 4X4 m (grafted), or 7X7 m (propagated by seed).
Prune during winter the dried, dead crowded branches from trees.
Remove the false branches and water shoots to prevent infection and spread of disease.
Don’t plant maize and cucurbits’ vine inside citrus orchard.
Spray diluated cattle urine in water in a ratio of 1:5 for 2-3 times on tree in an interval of 5 days at the time of new flushings.
Orchard sanitation should be maintained through removing infested leaves and shoots.
Avoid growing in locations showing high historical infection rates.
Monitoring: Monitor during rainy season weekly the whitish powdery growth on leaves, twigs, stem and fruit.
Disease is more prevalent at high temperature and humidity.
At high infestation, pale whitish-grey-green, twisted, upward curled defoliated young leaves may be seen.
In severe conditions, the symptoms in the tree like dieback of young shoots and dropping of greyish coloured immature fruits are observed.
Consider action if more than 5% of twigs sampled are affected.
Direct Control: Prune the diseased plant parts and destroy them (e.g. by burning).
Spray sulphur 80% WP @ 2g/L of water, repeat after 10-15 days.
Spray dinocap (48% EC) @ 2ml/L of water, repeat after 10-15 days.
Restrictions: Apply above mentioned fungicides alternately to prevent resistance and while spraying, foliage must be thoroughly wet.
When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
